The design of this course is settled and its material is being built: the slides of the three days, the scripts that build the analysis file from the raw files, and the reproduction of each of the five reanalyses. Until they are ready, the pages of the course link to the material that exists, and the [slides page](slides.qmd) shows the deck of the earlier three-day course.

This is the three-day course on the EU-frames case, a study of Eurobarometer surveys in the *European Sociological Review*, which asked whether the economic crisis changed how citizens of the European Union frame the Union. The course starts from scratch and takes the claim of the original author (OA) from the raw data to a preregistered analysis of your own. Day 1 introduces open research and the infrastructures on which it rests, the aims and the methods of SCORE and Multi100, and the paper in detail, and ends with the tools installed and the data downloaded. Day 2 teaches R and an IDE on the data of the case, builds the analysis file from the raw files as an exercise in data management, and reproduces the result of one of the five reanalyses, chosen by each participant, with the time to understand every line of the code that produced it. Day 3 turns to robustness: the choices that lie between the data and a result, the curve of 864 specifications of the claim, and an analysis of your own design, preregistered before it runs and added to the class chart.

## How you work

The course is taught in R, in an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.) on your own machine and in the downloadable workspace of the case, both of which day 1 installs. Unlike the one-day courses, it starts from the raw Eurobarometer files, which you download yourself on day 1 from the GESIS archive, under a free account and on terms that do not allow the files to be passed on, so that the files never leave your machine. Each day has a page that lists its four sessions in order, with buttons into the modules, the case pages and the tasks of the workspace on which each session works.

## The days of the course

- **[Before the course](before.qmd)** (about two to three hours). You read the case study and the paper, and create the account that the raw files need.
- **[Day 1 – Open research and the case](day-1.qmd)** (four sessions of ninety minutes). The day covers credibility and the three Rs, repositories and data sources, SCORE and Multi100, and the paper in detail, and it ends with the tools installed and the data downloaded.
- **[Day 2 – Tools and the reproduction](day-2.qmd)** (four sessions of ninety minutes). You learn R and the IDE on the data of the case, build the analysis file from the raw files, and reproduce one of the five reanalyses, which you report and send to the class.
- **[Day 3 – Robustness and the multiverse](day-3.qmd)** (four sessions of ninety minutes). You write the estimand statement and the causal graph, work through the specification menu and the methods behind it, and design an analysis of your own, which you preregister, run and place on the curve.
- **[After the course](after.qmd)** (as long as you like). The page says where to go next.

[Start with Before the course](before.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
